name: Fiery Rose
lede: Fiery Rose is a hot, saturated pink-red from Crayola's crayon list, close enough to Neon Fuchsia and Begonia Rose that only a careful eye tells them apart, and too bright for any painting in our archive to match.

sections.title: A Crayola pink
sections.body:
Wikipedia's color lists carry Fiery Rose at #FF5470 and credits Crayola as the source [1]. Measured against the ISCC-NBS block system it falls nearest to block 3, "deep pink," though 5.4 units off that block's center, which is why the name reads as its own shade rather than a textbook pink [2]. In Munsell terms it sits near 2.3R 6.0/15.5: very high chroma, tipped slightly toward orange [2].

Two neighbors mark the edges of the same small patch of color space. [[neon-fuchsia|Neon Fuchsia]] sits 2.9 units away and reads more vivid; [[begonia-rose|Begonia Rose]] sits 3.2 units away and reads duller [2]. Crayola's own Radical Red lands close enough to confuse without a swatch in hand [1]. Who coined "Fiery Rose," and when, is undocumented here [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a match for Fiery Rose, as photographed [3]. That says more about the archive than the color: oil and tempera pigments, even fresh and unvarnished, rarely reach the saturation a modern print color can hold [3].
